conviction_note: Event is real and confirmed. The differentiated find is that Imperial quietly disposed of a 160,000 dwt suezmax with no press release and no 6-K, leaving year-over-year fleet deadweight flat (1,195,000 -> 1,197,000 dwt) against a 27% larger share count, while the forward rate deck (MR/LR1 mid-$20k/day vs a $49,551/day Q2 average) and $130m of remaining vessel obligations make the print's forward content worse than its backward content; that is set against a near-certain record Q2 and a +17.8% run-up, netting to a modest sell-the-news.

findings.finding: Imperial sold its 2007-built 160,000 dwt suezmax Suez Enchanted for ~$49m with no press release and no 6-K, so year-over-year fleet deadweight is flat (1,195,000 dwt in the 2025-09-05 boilerplate vs 1,197,000 dwt in the 2026-09-04 boilerplate, +0.17%) while basic shares went from ~35.6m (Q2 2025: $12.8m net income / $0.36 EPS) to 45.21m, i.e. per-share carrying capacity fell ~21% in a year.
findings.why_not_priced: The company issued a dedicated press release when it BOUGHT these two suezmaxes in 2022 and when it SOLD its aframax in 2023, but issued none here; EDGAR shows no 6-K at all between 2026-05-22 and 2026-08-28, and the 2026-08-28 6-K is only the proxy plus 2025 audited statements. The only public traces are a paywalled shipping trade item and a changed line in the 'About Imperial Petroleum' boilerplate. If the market had processed it, StockTitan's headline on the 2026-09-04 release would not read 'A 25-vessel fleet could follow contracted ship purchases at Imperial Petroleum' - the aggregators read a disposal as growth. Management also said nothing about any vessel sale on the 2026-05-22 Q1 call, so the disposal post-dates every piece of coverage the market has.
findings.independence: The boilerplate diff itself is a second, independent confirmation of the same disposal: 2026-05-19 says 'twenty-one vessels on the water - seven M.R. product tankers, two suezmax tankers, four handysize drybulk carriers...approximately 1,324,000 dwt' (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/19/3297643/0/en/Imperial-Petroleum-Inc-Announces-the-Date-for-the-Release-of-the-First-Qurarter-2026-Financial-and-Operating-Results-Conference-Call-and-Webcast.html) versus 2026-09-04 'one suezmax tanker, five handysize...approximately 1,197,000 dwt' (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/04/3356593/0/en/imperial-petroleum-inc-announces-the-date-for-the-release-of-the-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-financial-and-operating-results-conference-call-and-webcast.html). Share count 45.21m from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/impp/statistics/ (2026-09-09); the ~35.6m 2025 base is derived from the 2025-09-05 Q2 2025 release. NOTE: finding 3 below reads a different number off the same two boilerplates and should be treated as one source cluster with this one.
findings.note_direction: Two-sided: $49m is ~20% of the $243.7m market cap and the ship cost ~$23.4m in 2022, so a ~$25-30m book gain lands in Q3. Against that, management said suezmax spot averaged 'nearly $95,000' a day in Q1 2026, so this was the highest-earning asset in the fleet and Vafias sold it into the top.

findings.finding: The forward half of tomorrow's print is materially worse than the backward half: MR and LR1 spot was assessed at mid-$20k/day in late July against a $49,551/day Q2 2026 MR average, and management disclosed on the Q1 call that $130m of vessel purchase obligations remain ($52m due through end of Q3 2026, $78m by end-2026/early-2027) against $212.6m of cash - so the retail 'cash exceeds market cap' premise is roughly 60% pre-spent.
findings.why_not_priced: IMPP has zero sell-side coverage (stockanalysis.com shows no analysts), so there is no preview, no consensus and no published net-cash-after-commitments figure for this name; the $130m obligation schedule exists only inside a Q1 conference-call transcript, not in any press release or aggregator field. If it were priced, the stock would not have run +17.8% in twenty sessions into a quarter whose sequential follow-through is a halving of the rate that drives seven of its eight tankers, and the widely-shared retail write-up would not still be quoting an unencumbered ~$246m cash pile.
findings.independence: Separate confirmation of the capex schedule and the cash figure from the company's own Q1 2026 call, a different document and different publisher: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/22/impp-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-05-22), where management says '$52 million is expected to be paid through the end of Q3 26, while the remaining $78 million is due by the end of 26 or early 27'. Also independent: cash of $212.6m at 2026-03-31 was essentially unchanged from $212.2m at 2025-06-30 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/05/3145289/0/en/Imperial-Petroleum-Inc-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Six-Months-2025-Financial-and-Operating-Results.html), i.e. a year of record earnings produced no cash build.

findings.finding: The vessel delivery schedule management committed to has already failed: the 2026-05-19 boilerplate had 21 vessels on the water and five contracted for delivery 'by end of Q3 26', and the 2026-09-04 boilerplate still shows 21 on the water with four still contracted - one handysize arrived in three and a half months, with three weeks of Q3 left.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing aggregates a company's own boilerplate against the same boilerplate four months earlier, and the release that carries it is filed as a routine date announcement that no wire service reads for content. If the slippage were priced there would be coverage of a delayed fleet ramp; instead the only headline written about this release describes fleet growth to 25 ships.
findings.independence: Shares the same two boilerplate documents as finding 1 - treat as one source cluster. Corroborating but non-independent: management's 'five more vessels contracted for delivery through Q3 2026' on https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/22/impp-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-05-22).

findings.finding: Q2 2026 is arithmetically near-certain to be Imperial's best quarter ever by a wide margin - Q1 2026 delivered $28.0m net income and $0.60 EPS on an average 19.88 vessels with only about one month of the rate spike, whereas Q2 ran ~21 vessels with MR spot averaging $49,551/day, both suezmaxes on spot in a record crude market, and supramax averaging above $17,000/day (best since 2022), against a Q2 2025 base of $36.3m revenue and $12.8m net income - and no equity offering has been filed since the 2025-12-01 424B5.
findings.why_not_priced: With no analyst coverage there is no consensus EPS for IMPP, so no one has published the per-share arithmetic that a quarter of roughly $1.00-1.30 of EPS on a $5.335 stock implies; 'tanker rates were good' is the sector framing and does not convey that magnitude. The absence of dilution is checkable only on EDGAR: for a serial issuer, three and a half months with no 424B5 and no 6-K between 2026-05-22 and 2026-08-28 removes the single most reliable historical bear catalyst on this name.
findings.independence: Peer confirmation from different companies and different publishers that Q2 2026 was an all-time record tanker quarter: Scorpio Tankers record Q2 profit and $1.3bn net cash (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/scorpio-tankers-q2-2026-slides-record-profit-13b-net-cash-93CH-4824617) and Teekay Tankers record quarterly adjusted earnings on historic-high spot rates (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/08/03/teekay-tankers-q2-earnings-call-highlights.html, 2026-08-03). EDGAR filing index for the no-offering point: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001876581.json.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whether the C3is Inc. (CISS) investment forces a Q2 write-down at Imperial - Imperial's 13D/A of 2026-08-28 shows its as-converted stake fell from 90.2% to 80.5% after C3is's $6m July offering and three reverse splits in eight months (1-for-20 Jan, 1-for-7 Apr, 1-for-40 Aug 2026), but I could not source the carrying value of the C3is preferred on Imperial's balance sheet or its measurement basis, so I could not size any impairment and dropped it
Any company press release or 6-K disclosing the suezmax sale - none exists; EDGAR shows no 6-K between 2026-05-22 and 2026-08-28 and the imperialpetro.com press-release page returns 403

The Harry Vafias Form 4 of 2026-08-21 - it is a compensation grant (149,502 shares plus 149,502 options at $3.01, 50% vested 2026-08-08), not an open-market purchase, so it carries no information about his view of the print
Related-party vessel transactions with StealthGas or other Vafias entities in 2026 - the buyer of Suez Enchanted is not disclosed in the trade press and no affiliate transaction was findable
A dividend or expanded-buyback signal - no dividend discussion on the Q1 call and no announcement since; the $10m buyback was only $3.8m executed through 2026-05-21 and I found no update

An updated management NAV press release since 2025-12-22 ($508.03m, $11.38/share outstanding, $9.21 fully diluted); management said 'close to $13' on the Q1 call, so the NAV discount is already spoken and is not a new fact
Job postings, app reviews, status pages and customer forums - not applicable to a Greek FPI shipowner with no consumer surface
baseline_tension: There is no option chain and therefore no skew to agree or disagree with, and the baseline's 8-event history is not an earnings base rate at all - only three of those dates are real prints (2025-12-01 -2.35%, 2026-03-06 +8.50%, 2026-05-22 -2.46%), the rest are vessel, offering and proxy 6-Ks, and the 2026-08-28 'print' is the annual-meeting proxy plus 2025 audited statements; what my findings do cut against is the +17.8% twenty-day run-up, because the most relevant precedent on this name is a 'second best quarter in its history' headline that produced -2.46%.
